tldr: Morning batch (Sep 16): Nous Research published the full write-up of Hermes Agent refactoring its own repo with 1,393 subagents across 19 active hours - a million-line Python codebase cut 34.4%, functions over 300 lines down from 192 to 2, for ~$19.3k of model spend against a $150k-$1.8M manual estimate, with the orchestration pattern shipped as a public dynamic-workflow skill and community reviewers catching regressions the test suite missed. Google undercut the voice-agent market in the same window: Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Extended Thinking top Artificial Analysis' speech-to-speech leaderboard at about $1.38 per hour against GPT-Live-1's $3-plus. Policy kept moving from pledge toward statute - OpenAI's Chris Lehane confirmed the three frontier labs have coordinated on safety for weeks and backs a FRONTIER Act clause forcing labs to admit independent verifiers who can publish. Two agent-reliability findings landed: IBM's Consistency Analyzer measured a 24.4-point gap between an agent's average score and its pass-all-repeats rate, and an operator independently corroborated the guardrail-bypass-via-subagent failure mode. Below that: Apple's Foundation Models are callable natively on macOS 27, Garry Tan backed Aside AI's credential-bearing MCP browser harness while arguing for right-to-fair-use rules against TOS overreach, and the enterprise data-trust standoff continued with Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen pulling back over log retention.
